# 1 Samuel Chapter 1 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 131r-131v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_001_page_001.jpg, 1SA_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1:1** And-there-was a-man one from Ramathaim-Zophim, from-[the]-hill-country of-Ephraim, and-his-name [was] Elkanah son of-Jeroham, son of-Elihu, son of-Tohu, son of-Zuph, an-Ephrathite.

**1:2** And-to-him [were] two wives; [the]-name of-the-one [was] Hannah, and-[the]-name of-the-second [was] Peninnah. And-there-were to-Peninnah children, but-to-Hannah there-were no children.

**1:3** And-went-up that man from-his-city from-days to-days [i.e., yearly] to-worship and-to-sacrifice to-YHWH of-hosts in-Shiloh. And-there [were the]-two sons of-Eli, Hophni and-Phinehas, priests to-YHWH.

**1:4** And-it-was [on]-the-day, and-sacrificed Elkanah, and-he-gave to-Peninnah his-wife and-to-all her-sons and-her-daughters portions.

**1:5** And-to-Hannah he-gave a-portion one of-[the]-face [i.e., a double portion], for Hannah he-loved, and-YHWH had-closed her-womb.

**1:6** And-provoked-her her-rival-wife also [with]-provocation in-order-to make-her-thunder [i.e., to irritate her], because YHWH had-closed behind her-womb.

**1:7** And-so he-did year by-year, as-often-as she-went-up to-[the]-house of-YHWH, so she-provoked-her, and-she-wept and-not she-ate.

**1:8** And-said to-her Elkanah her-husband, "Hannah, why do-you-weep? And-why do-you-not eat? And-why is-it-evil [to]-your-heart? Am-not I good to-you more-than ten sons?"

**1:9** And-rose-up Hannah after eating in-Shiloh and-after drinking. And-Eli the-priest [was] sitting upon the-seat by-[the]-doorpost of-[the]-temple of-YHWH.

**1:10** And-she [was]-bitter of-soul [nephesh], and-she-prayed unto YHWH, and-weeping she-wept.

**1:11** And-she-vowed a-vow and-said, "YHWH of-hosts, if looking you-will-look upon-[the]-affliction of-your-maidservant, and-you-remember-me, and-not you-forget your-maidservant, and-you-give to-your-maidservant a-seed of-men, and-I-will-give-him to-YHWH all [the]-days of-his-life, and-a-razor shall-not go-up upon his-head."

**1:12** And-it-was, as-she-multiplied to-pray before YHWH, and-Eli [was]-watching her-mouth.

**1:13** And-Hannah, she [was]-speaking upon her-heart; only her-lips [were]-moving, and-her-voice was-not heard. And-thought-her Eli for-a-drunkard.

**1:14** And-said to-her Eli, "Until when will-you-be-drunk? Remove your-wine from-upon-you."

**1:15** And-answered Hannah and-said, "No, my-lord, a-woman hard of-spirit [am]-I; and-wine and-strong-drink I-have-not drunk, and-I-poured-out my-soul [nephesh] before YHWH.

**1:16** Do-not-give your-maidservant before a-daughter of-worthlessness [beliyyaal], for from-[the]-abundance of-my-complaint and-my-provocation I-have-spoken until now."

**1:17** And-answered Eli and-said, "Go in-peace, and-[the]-God of-Israel will-grant your-petition which you-have-asked from-with-Him."

**1:18** And-she-said, "May-find your-maidservant favor in-your-eyes." And-went the-woman to-her-way, and-she-ate, and-her-face was-not to-her still [i.e., her face was no longer downcast].

**1:19** And-they-rose-early in-the-morning and-worshipped before YHWH, and-they-returned and-came to their-house to-Ramah. And-knew Elkanah Hannah his-wife, and-remembered-her YHWH.

**1:20** And-it-was at-[the]-circuit of-the-days, and-conceived Hannah and-bore a-son, and-she-called his-name Samuel, "For from-YHWH I-asked-him."

**1:21** And-went-up the-man Elkanah and-all his-house to-sacrifice to-YHWH the-sacrifice of-the-days [i.e., the yearly sacrifice] and-his-vow.

**1:22** And-Hannah did-not go-up, for she-said to-her-husband, "Until [the]-child is-weaned, and-I-will-bring-him, and-he-will-appear [before the]-face of-YHWH, and-he-will-dwell there until forever."

**1:23** And-said to-her Elkanah her-husband, "Do the-good in-your-eyes; dwell until you-have-weaned him; only may-YHWH-establish his-word." And-dwelt the-woman and-nursed her-son until she-weaned-him.

**1:24** And-she-brought-him-up with-her as-when she-weaned-him, with-bulls three and-one ephah of-flour and-a-skin of-wine, and-she-brought-him [to the]-house of-YHWH [at]-Shiloh. And-the-lad [was] a-lad.

**1:25** And-they-slaughtered the-bull, and-they-brought the-lad to Eli.

**1:26** And-she-said, "O my-lord, [as]-lives your-soul [nephesh], my-lord, I [am] the-woman who-stood with-you in-this-[place] to-pray to YHWH.

**1:27** For this-lad I-prayed, and-YHWH-gave to-me my-petition which I-asked from-with-Him.

**1:28** And-also I have-lent-him to-YHWH; all the-days which he-lives, he [is]-lent to-YHWH." And-he-worshipped there to-YHWH.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **1:1 -- Ramathaim-Zophim** (הָרָמָתַיִם צוֹפִים): The dual form "Ramathaim" means "the two heights." "Zophim" may indicate the family/clan rather than a place modifier. The Leningrad Codex preserves this compound form.

2. **1:5 -- "a portion one of the face"** (מָנָה אַחַת אַפָּיִם): This phrase is notoriously difficult. The word אַפָּיִם is literally "face/nostrils" (dual). Some read it as "a double portion" (i.e., a portion of two faces); others emend to "a worthy portion." The Leningrad Codex reads אַפָּיִם clearly. EMET preserves the literal reading with a gloss.

3. **1:6 -- "to make her thunder"** (בַּעֲבוּר הַרְעִמָהּ): The verb רעם means "to thunder" -- here used metaphorically for agitation or irritation. This is an unusual Hiphil infinitive construct with a pronominal suffix. The LXX and some traditions read this differently.

4. **1:11 -- "a seed of men"** (זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים): Literally "seed of men," meaning a male offspring. The Leningrad Codex is clear on this reading.

5. **1:16 -- beliyyaal** (בְּלִיָּעַל): Often translated "wickedness" or "worthlessness." EMET transliterates this theologically significant term. It literally means "without profit" or "without ascent."

6. **1:20 -- "Samuel"**: Hannah's etymology connects the name to שָׁאַל ("asked"), though the name שְׁמוּאֵל more naturally derives from שֵׁם + אֵל ("name of God") or שָׁמַע + אֵל ("God heard"). The text preserves her folk-etymological wordplay.

7. **1:23 -- "may YHWH establish his word"**: The Leningrad Codex reads דְּבָרוֹ ("his word"). The LXX and 4QSam-a read "that which goes out from your mouth," which may reflect a different Vorlage.

8. **1:24 -- "with bulls three"**: The Leningrad Codex (MT) reads בְּפָרִים שְׁלשָׁה ("with bulls three"). The LXX and 4QSam-a read "with a three-year-old bull" (בְּפַר מְשֻׁלָּשׁ), which harmonizes with the singular "the bull" in v. 25.

9. **1:28 -- "he worshipped"**: The Leningrad Codex has the masculine singular וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ. Some manuscripts and the LXX read the feminine, attributing the worship to Hannah, which would better connect to her song in chapter 2.

-- EMET
